cards.text: Way out in the land of Uz, there's a man named Job. Before the Bible tells us one thing that happens to him, it tells us what kind of man he is. So lean in, friend.

cards.question: Job lives in the land of Uz. How does the Bible describe him?

cards.text: Job has seven sons and three daughters. TEN kids! I had six cookie cutters on one counter and I STILL lost track of Chip.

And the man is LOADED: 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 yoke of oxen, 500 female donkeys and a very large number of servants. Meanwhile I spent years in a junk drawer, and the nicest thing I owned was a crumb.

cards.question: With all those animals and servants, Job is the greatest man of all the people of the East.

cards.text: Job's sons take turns holding feasts in their homes, and they invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them. Taking turns? Friend, the dead batteries I shared that drawer with couldn't even take turns TALKING.

cards.question: When the days of feasting are over, Job sends for his children and rises early in the morning. What does he do for them?

answers.text: Gives each of them a flock
Throws a feast of his own

cards.question: Why does Job offer burnt offerings after his children's feasts?

answers.text: He thinks they may have sinned
A priest has told him to
He made a vow to God

cards.question: Job offers burnt offerings for his children only once, after the very first feast.

cards.text: Now the scene moves. One day the sons of God come to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan comes with them.

cards.question: The LORD asks Satan, "Where have you come from?" What does Satan say?

answers.text: From the depths of the sea

cards.text: Walking back and forth in the earth, like the guy at work who paces the hallway all day and never ONCE sits at his desk. Then the LORD brings up Job by name.

cards.question: The LORD tells Satan there is no one on earth like Job.
Satan asks, "Does Job fear God for nothing?" He says God has put a hedge around Job and blessed the work of his hands. What is Satan saying about Job?

answers.text: Job fears God only because God blesses him
Job deserves even more blessing from God
Job has been hiding his sins from God

cards.text: Then Satan goes for it. He tells the LORD to stretch out His hand and strike all that Job has.

cards.question: Satan says if everything Job has is struck, Job will surely ___ God to His face.

cards.text: The LORD answers, "Very well," and tells Satan that everything Job has is in his hands.

cards.question: The LORD also lets Satan lay a hand on Job himself.

cards.text: Then Satan goes out from the presence of the LORD. Friend, this is the part where I'd set the oven timer and hold my breath.
One day, Job's sons and daughters are eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house. Then a messenger comes to Job.

cards.question: The first messenger says Job's oxen were plowing and his donkeys were grazing nearby. Then what happened to them?

answers.text: They ran off into the desert

cards.text: Raiders called the Sabeans swooped down, took the animals and put the servants to the sword. And the messenger says, "I alone have escaped to tell you!"

cards.question: The first messenger is still speaking to Job. What happens next?
The second messenger reports on Job's sheep. What happened to them?

answers.text: Fire fell from heaven and burned them
Raiders drove them away to the north
Wild animals scattered them in the night

cards.text: He says, "The fire of God fell from heaven." It burned up the sheep and the servants, and then that line again: "I alone have escaped to tell you!"

cards.question: He's STILL speaking, and here comes a third messenger. Raiders formed three bands and took Job's ___.

cards.text: The Chaldeans raided the camels and put the servants to the sword. And one more time: "I alone have escaped to tell you!"

cards.question: While the third messenger is still speaking, a fourth one comes to Job. Who is this news about?
Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house. What does the fourth messenger say struck the house?

answers.text: A mighty wind from the desert
A great shaking of the ground

cards.text: The house collapsed on the young people, and they are dead. And the messenger says, "I alone have escaped to tell you!"
Four messengers, one right after another. Then Job stands up, tears his robe and shaves his head.

cards.question: Job has torn his robe and shaved his head. What does he do next?

answers.text: Falls to the ground and worships
Leaves the land of Uz for good

cards.text: And Job says, "Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I will return."

cards.question: Job says he came from his mother's womb naked and will return naked. What does he mean?

answers.text: He came with nothing and will leave with nothing
He is ashamed to stand before God now
He wants to start his whole life over

cards.question: Job says, "The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away." What does Job do with the name of the LORD?
In all this, Job sins by charging God with wrongdoing.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave Job for now. Hang on, friend, because this story is far from done.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. The two wrong answers share an 'X but Y' shape with a flaw attached, and 'Blameless and upright' is the only purely positive answer and the only one that sounds like Bible wording.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke 'I STILL lost track of Chip' invents a new moment in the Millers' kitchen. That is new backstory, not a small moment around his bakery. It also cuts against the backstory, where he looked after the cutters closely.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Job has seven sons and three daughters.' 'TEN kids!' 'I had six cookie cutters...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Job's sons take turns...' 'Taking turns?' 'Friend, the dead batteries...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 8 asks why Job offers burnt offerings 'after his children's feasts' (plural). Card 7 also says 'When the days of feasting are over.' Together these tell the baker the offerings happen again and again, which gives away the answer to card 9 ('only once, after the very first feast' is False).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Satan appears here for the first time, and no card says simply who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card cites Job 1:13, but its last sentence ('Then a messenger comes to Job.') tells Job 1:14. The citation is too narrow and should be Job 1:13-14.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'He's STILL speaking.' 'He' points back to the second messenger from a card that is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
